activity_summary: You crossed the close with Mistress Ansell and Gillis Verbeke and stood in the porch of St Helen's before morning prayer. Master Thwaite promised fourteen heads and two turnings of the glass. The sixpence for firing and washing runs till Lady Day, and the worn poem from Paul's is still under the cat.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Walked over with the household and took the draughty end of the bench.

entities.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell
entities.context: Kept the mud outside, named the sixpence till Lady Day, and wanted quiet after nine.

entities.name: Master Josias Thwaite
entities.context: Greeted the porch and set fourteen heads on the epistle.

entities.name: Gillis Verbeke
entities.context: Answered for the loom, and took the bench by the pillar.

facets.activity: Stood in the porch before morning prayer

quotes.speaker: josias_thwaite
quotes.text: I have divided the epistle into fourteen heads today, that no man may go to his salt herring unexamined.

quotes.speaker: dorcas_ansell
quotes.text: The sixpence runs till Lady Day, and then the sun may warm him for nothing.

quotes.speaker: william_shakespeare
quotes.text: I never miss a fourteenthly, sir.
